postTitle: How Much Can You Borrow? Home and Car Loan Rules of Thumb, Tested
topic: Which pay is the rule using? The same payment is a third of pay before tax and 45% of take home pay

assumptions.notes: Blog example (Marcus): €54,000 a year before tax (€4,500 a month), about €3,300 a month after tax. Payment on the bank's €330,000 at 3.5% over 30 years: about €1,482 a month = 32.9% of €4,500 (shown 33%) and 44.9% of €3,300 (shown 45%; the lesson says about 45%). Numbers in the reel: €1,482, 33%, 45%.

hookVariants.narration: Same payment: a third of your pay, or almost half? It depends which pay you count.

beats.narration: Marcus pays about one thousand four hundred and eighty euros a month.
Against his pay before tax, it is a third.
Against what reaches his account after tax, it is forty five percent.
Many rules use pay before tax. Bills come from take home pay.

The same mortgage payment: a third of your pay, or almost half? It depends on which pay you count.

Marcus pays about €1,482 a month. Against his pay before tax, that is 33%. Against what reaches his account after tax and contributions, it is 45%. Many borrowing rules use pay before tax; bills are paid from take home pay. Many people check which one a rule means.
